fixes.explanation: Paddan-aram is where Jacob lived with Laban for years (Genesis 31:41), and most of his sons were born there (Genesis 35:26). That's Jacob's story, though. Esau's sons were "…born to him in the land of Canaan." (Genesis 36:5) Easy to cross the wires with two brothers and two sets of kids.

You got it, baker. Verse 8 says, "So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the area of Mount Seir." (Genesis 36:8) And look at who's already there. Verse 20 lists the sons of Seir the Horite, "…who were living in the land…" (Genesis 36:20) So Esau doesn't move into an empty lot. He shows up with all his stuff and finds neighbors. I know that feeling. I once got a new drawer-mate with a full set of dead batteries and zero warning.

Mount Sinai matters a lot later in the Bible. The LORD comes down on it in Exodus 19:18-20, and He gives the Ten Commandments in Exodus 20:1-17. But it's not where Esau settled. Verse 8 says, "So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the area of Mount Seir." (Genesis 36:8) Sinai and Seir both start with S. That's about as far as the match goes.
